title: Reconcile asynchronous fragment consumption across retries and multipart requests
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Problem summary: The metering pipeline can over- or under-count consumption when clients send large inputs as multipart fragments, then reconnect/retry, or when midstream model switches (fallback/variant selection) occur. Root causes observed so far: lack of a durable, globally-unique fragment id that survives client retries; replayed fragments being credited again in the aggregation layer; rate-limiter enforcement applied at the fragment ingestion boundary without correlating to overall request id; and inconsistent handling of prefix/kv-cache carryover which changes output token counts reported to billing. This ticket plans reconciliation logic, idempotency markers, and audit tooling to ensure token counts and quota decrements are correct across the streaming/resume/multipart surface.
acceptance_criteria: Metering must not double-credit tokens for replayed or retried fragments in any of the documented failure/reconnect scenarios.
A durable fragment id (or equivalent idempotency key) is attached to fragments and persisted to the metering store before consumption is counted.
Rate limiting and quota checks must operate on logical request scope (request+fragments) where applicable, with clear fallback behavior for partial quota consumption.

Automated test harness reproduces: intermittent client disconnects with replay, multipart uploads with overlapping byte ranges, midstream model switch to fallback variant, and client-side resumed sessions — all validating final billed token counts match expected baselines.
New dashboard panels and an automated regression alert detect >=0.5% deviation in daily streaming token counts vs trace-level reconciled counts for a given customer.
Backward-compatible rollout: feature gated with runtime flag; safe rollback path documented.
tasks: Design: finalize fragment id format (opaque UUID vs derived hash) and required metadata fields (request_id, sequence_number, client_session_id).
Spec: update ingestion API contract to accept optional idempotency_fragment_id and sequence_number with semantics for replay detection.
Implementation: persist fragment id to metering primary (append-only) before invoking charge calculation.
Implementation: modify aggregator to dedupe by (customer, request_id, fragment_id) and correctly attribute tokens to input vs output.
Rate limiting: change quota check to consider pending fragments crediting and implement partial-consumption semantics + quota reservation TTL.
Testing: add unit tests for dedupe logic and integration tests for resume/replay scenarios in the staging metering environment.
Observability: add end-to-end trace tags, dashboards, and a reconcile job that periodically audits streamed sessions for anomalies.
Documentation: update developer docs and public API notes describing fragment id behavior and best practices for clients.
Rollout: feature gate, staged rollout on canary customers, monitor dashboards and engage rollback if discrepancy > 0.2%.
Postmortem: collect data for 7 days and produce a short report with any residual edge cases and proposed follow-ups.
test_plan: Unit: dedupe algorithm tests with duplicate fragment sequences, out-of-order fragments, and missing sequence numbers.
Integration: controlled replay test where client sends fragments 1..N, disconnects after M, reconnects and resends M..N; assert billed tokens == baseline single-send.
Integration: multipart overlapping-uploads test (simulate clients that split at different byte boundaries) to confirm no double-counting.
Integration: midstream model switch test where fallback variant produces different token lengths; ensure attribution is to final chosen model with a reconciliation record of the switch.
Load: synthetic load test with 10k concurrent streaming sessions including 5% reconnects to verify dedupe store performance and throughput impact.
E2E: run the reconcile job nightly in staging and assert zero net drift for known deterministic traces.
Alerting: create an alert for reconcile-job failure and for >0.2% discrepancy between metered and reconciled token counts per-customer over 24h.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Ticket created by Daniel Kim: initial investigation after ops report showing weekend spike in streaming token counts for three customers.
2026-03-04 - Repro steps captured by Aisha: local harness reproduced replay double-count when fragment id absent; attached sample trace IDs.

2026-03-06 - Design sync: decided to use opaque UUID fragment ids generated by client when available, otherwise server will generate stable IDs derived from (request_id, fragment_hash, client_session_id). Trade-off: client opt-in reduces server work but we need robust server fallback.
2026-03-08 - Spike PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/meters/pull/842 implementing persistent fragment id column and dedupe index (WIP).
2026-03-10 - Rate limit design: team agreed on quota reservation TTL of 45s for pending fragments; if session never completes, reservation expires and reconciler refunds partial reservations.
2026-03-12 - Observability: dashboard prototypes up in Grafana showing reconciled vs raw counts (panel ids: stream_reconciled_vs_raw, per_customer_drift).
2026-03-14 - Implementation progress: dedupe layer merged behind feature flag in staging, integration tests passing for low-volume cases. Performance bench scheduled 2026-03-16.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Dedupe store adds write/read latency and increases load on metering primary. Mitigation: use small append-only table with TTL, add memcache layer for hot session ids, bench under load before rollout.

Risk: Clients that do not send fragment ids will rely on server-generated ids which could differ across retries if not careful. Mitigation: define deterministic server id derivation and include sample code in SDKs.

Risk: Partial quota reservation may reduce available capacity for high-concurrency customers. Mitigation: keep TTL conservative (45s), expose quota reservation metrics, and allow tenant-level reservation limits.
Risk: Reconciliation job complexity and cost. Mitigation: implement incremental reconcile for recent windows and fall back to sampling for long tails.
notes: Found three customer cases where clients used older SDKs that chunked payloads differently; contributed to observed drift.
Runtime flag name: metering.fragment_dedupe_v1; default off in production until we've run canary cohort for 48h.
Consider follow-up: metric to expose per-request reconciliation status so SRE/support can quickly confirm billing correctness for escalations.
